selected.item: Gemini 4 Hydrogen (gemini-4-hydrogen): Google's fast, cost-efficient Gemini 4 model for everyday coding and agentic workflows, generally available on November 12, 2026. 1M-token input context and up to 1M output tokens; the upgrade path from Gemini 3.8 Flash. Four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default) and a new xhigh. Flat pricing of $1.50 per 1M input tokens and $7.50 per 1M output tokens across the whole 1M-token context; a free tier is available. Available in Google AI Studio (all tiers), the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search for all users globally, and Google Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers; it is the default model for the Antigravity agent in Gemini Managed Agents. Vendor-reported: 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at the high default setting; Terminal-Bench 4.1 57% vs 18.2%; fabricated claims cut by more than 5x; Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 51 at default high and 54 at xhigh vs 50 for Gemini 4 Argon; Agent Arena #5; HLE-Diamond 58.8% (class lead); Vals Tax Agent Bench #1 (52.3%); Vals Legal Research Bench tied #1 (55.8%); AutomationBench-AA class lead; Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark 53.4%; Agents' Last Exam v1.1 71.6%. Orchestrator in Antigravity dynamically switches between Carbon and Hydrogen; on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it reached near-Carbon success with 24% less quota and 19% faster completion. Safety: overreach in agentic tasks down up to 81%, under-service down up to 79%, misaligned actions and task shortcutting down 12x, 96.7% honesty on the internal agent honesty evaluation, 99.9% chain-of-thought legibility, 2.3x more resilient to indirect prompt injection on Gray Swan IPI. All performance figures are Google's own, not independent verification.
selected.note: The Google blog post is dated November 12, 2026 (published 19:30 UTC) and the Gemini API changelog entry is dated November 12, 2026. Both were read directly in this run. Not covered in earlier issues of this series.

selected.item: API inference residency in India for GPT-6 Luna (gpt-6-luna): OpenAI extended its India data residency from storage to processing. For eligible API projects, supported requests and the model computation that generates the response now take place in India, and supported customer content is stored there. Initially GPT-6 Luna only, through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs (text and image inputs, text output), for direct API use. Requires active Zero Data Retention (Modified Abuse Monitoring alone is insufficient); Standard pay-as-you-go only; hosted tools are unavailable for regional processing in India. Access via a new regional API project selecting India for storage and processing, endpoint in.api.openai.com. India joins Australia and Japan as the latest additions; the US, Europe and UAE already offer regional processing. Data-residency endpoints carry a 10% uplift for eligible models released on or after March 5, 2026.
selected.note: The November 12, 2026 announcement date is from OpenAI's press statement as reported by multiple outlets (PTI via The Hindu BusinessLine, Economic Times, Business Standard, Rediff). The capability itself is confirmed in OpenAI's API documentation (your-data guide), read directly in this run, which lists India (in.api.openai.com) with Storage Yes / Processing Yes for gpt-6-luna. The docs page carries no date.

selected.item: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents: Anthropic launched a self-hosted option for its Managed Agents service. Organizations run the whole Managed Agents service - not only self-hosted sandboxes - on their own infrastructure, and store agents, sessions and session history there. The server sends model requests to the provider of the organization's choice, Anthropic by default. Access is by request through the Anthropic account team. This is a deployment/service option, not a new model.
selected.note: Release-notes entry dated November 12, 2026, read directly in this run. Not covered in earlier issues of this series.

selected.item: Daybreak Defense Factory and Daybreak Red Team: OpenAI introduced two cybersecurity products at its 'Cyber at the Frontier' keynote on November 12, 2026 (10:00 PT, November 13 03:00 JST). Defense Factory uses AI agents to investigate vulnerabilities and prepare patches for review; Red Team tests web apps, validates vulnerabilities and verifies fixes with coordinated AI agents. Both start from an early-access application (Request Daybreak Access). GPT-6 Cyber, the cyber-specialized model behind this work, was covered in No.20 (November 5). Details beyond the keynote page are limited in this run.
selected.note: The keynote page was read directly in this run; it lists the two products and the early-access application but carries no date line. The keynote date and time (November 12, 10:00 PT) are from OpenAI's own keynote announcement. Not covered in earlier issues of this series.
